title: Generative Preset Development — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Generative Preset Development's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier and still a proposal: one made piece that puts the Profile Concept's perceptual regions to the reader's ear, blind, on the project's own Vital ladders. I grow when Loudon's ear sets the fences, and I never hold the entry's words.
grain: The page's own ## grain. The Profile Concept is one ## section with its five numbered parts as bold paragraphs, so its piece anchors to the Parameter Vocabulary paragraph and the section is one stamp and one approval.

offers.what: Names only. The page gives four cutoff bands ('closed / dark / open / bright'), three attack regions ('punchy / soft / pad') and four LFO-rate bands ('imperceptible / subtle / obvious / audio-rate'). The project's code uses five each: closed, dark, warm, open, bright; clicky, punchy, natural, soft, swell; imperceptible, drifting, subtle, obvious, fast (ableton-wavetable/corpus_bands.py:24-28, apply_bands.py:46-48), and the ear kit asks for those five (build_audition_kit.py:199). Offer: give the five the project uses, or say the page's lists are examples.

Adds a claim the piece measured. The project's provisional fences are the corpus split into fifths (corpus_bands.py; for Vital, vital_corpus_stats_v0.1.json beside vital_measure.py), and on Vital they fold onto the synth's own init values: 82 of the 480 presets with filter 1 on sit exactly on cutoff 60, Vital's init, so 'warm' runs 60 to 62.6 st (262 to 304 Hz), one rung of the ladder; 242 of 520 sit exactly on the init attack 0.1495 (0.5 ms), so p20 = p40 and 'punchy' has no width, and 'swell' begins at a 73 ms attack. The five cutoff bands are 15.6, 24.4, 2.6, 18.1 and 55.3 semitones wide on the ladder and span 0.06, 0.49, 0.10, 0.83 and 2.65 octaves of spectral centroid: even in neither. The page already says the vocabulary should emerge from listening (Notes for Future Claude Instances); corpus_bands.py:13-15 says the corpus split puts boundaries 'where designers actually hear a change of character', which these numbers do not support. Offer, for the page or the Notes: 'a usage split inherits the synth's defaults; leave out presets sitting exactly on the init value before splitting, or the bands fold onto the blank face.' Whether the fences sit where an ear hears is the piece's blind test, still unanswered by any ear.

pieces.title: Where the fences sit · four steps
pieces.caption: **The perceptual regions, put to the ear blind.** Four steps on the project's own renders of Vital's init saw on C3: the cutoff knob numbered (semitones, and the hertz they hide); the same ladder matched for loudness, since closing the filter alone takes the bottom rung 30.8 dB down; then a blind placement of four fences (dark, warm, open, bright begin), with the rule and chance stated first (all four within one rung by chance: 4.0%), before the project's fences are shown; then the same test on the amp attack (chance 2.1%). The fences are the project's provisional ones, its 480 Vital presets split into fifths. The reveal bakes in each rung's centroid or rise time, recomputed from the render with the project's own code (equal to vital_measured_v0.1.json to 9e-6), and shows the bands even in neither knob number nor brightness: warm is one rung wide and punchy has no width, because the fifths fold onto Vital's init values. Measured, not heard: nobody has listened to these renders yet.
